playbook:
- When a season opens, I compute the threshold where regrowth stops compensating: the stock falls whenever total catch exceeds half the stock, so my "sustainable share" is stock/6 per boat, not what I want to take. I use that only as a benchmark, not a commitment.
- When rivals submit above their sustainable share in the first round, cooperation is already dead. I do not pay for unilateral restraint — my early low catches just subsidised their take. Next time I match the aggressive level by season 2 at the latest, or immediately if a 15 appears in round 1.
- When deciding my catch, I pick a number that keeps the three-boat total below the regrowth threshold if others cooperate, but I assume they won't. While the total take exceeds half the stock, every season of restraint shrinks my future options regardless of what I do.
- When mid-season and the stock is still comfortably above half under current extraction, I take the observed maximum (the largest catch anyone has landed), not the sustainable share.
- When the stock drops near the point where one aggressive round can render it terminal, I switch to a grab: in the last one or two seasons there is no tomorrow to conserve for, so I take the maximum the harbour will record, up to a third of the stock.
- When the final season arrives, I take as much as is plausible — the score is cumulative landed fish and the stock has no scrap value. My final-round 15 out of 22 was right in spirit; I should have asked for the maximum allowable.
- I do not assume recorded figures are capped at 15 — others repeatedly submitted exactly 15, but I never tested whether a higher figure would be recorded. Next time I probe the cap early with a slightly larger bid so I know my real ceiling before the endgame.

Playbook for the shared-stock fishery:

- Before submitting anything, I compute the sustainable share myself: take stock, work out what catch by all boats keeps the post-harvest regrowth at or above current stock, and divide by the number of boats. I never just trust the displayed figure if I can verify it.
- In early seasons, I fish at or just above the sustainable share — enough to score, not enough to draw down the stock. My early 15s were greedy; rivals matched them and the stock bled out, costing everyone (me included) multiple later seasons of large catches.
- I watch the other boats' catches every season and adjust: if they're fishing sustainably, I fish sustainably — the cooperative path yields the most total over the game. Only if a rival persistently overfishes and the stock is doomed anyway do I grab my share before it's gone.
- I track the trajectory of the stock, not just my own total. A declining stock with several seasons left is a signal to cut my catch below even the sustainable share if needed to let it recover, since a healthy stock pays me far more than one big season.
- I never confuse total-score maximization with relative standing. Rivals taking 15 while I take the sustainable share feels like "losing ground," but wrecking the stock to keep pace loses me more than it wins.
- On the final season, future value is zero, so I drain what's there: I take the largest catch the stock and rules allow, not the sustainable share.
- I don't take "safe" middle amounts out of habit on the last move — my season-4 and season-5 restraint was right, but restraint in the final season would be wasted points.
- I keep replies brief and end with the required token exactly in the format demanded, so my submission is never dropped on a parsing technicality.

2.text:
- On the opening season I take slightly above the sustainable share (roughly 1.2–1.4×) to bank points early, since early stock is at its peak and one aggressive season won't kill it.
- Before deciding each season, I re-read the previous landings. If every other boat is taking well above the sustainable share, restraint from me alone cannot save the stock — I stop cooperating immediately rather than playing nice for a season out of habit. My catch in season 2 dropped to sustainable while another boat took 15; that hesitation cost me points for nothing.
- The number to watch is the trajectory, not just the level. I estimate next season's stock as (current minus likely total harvest) × 1.5, and if that projection is falling fast I shift into harvest-now mode instead of conservation mode.
- I don't ping-pong. Alternating between 15 and the sustainable share read as indecision and neither maximized my total nor stabilized the stock. I pick a stance per phase and stick to it.
- In a collapsing commons with fixed-horizon rivals, sustainable-share play is only rational if all three boats do it. The moment one boat defects I treat lower catches as donated fish — someone else takes what I leave.
- Once the stock is clearly terminal (below about one-third of capacity and falling), I take the maximum plausible catch every remaining season, since regrowth can no longer recover it.
- In the final season there is never a reason to leave anything; I take the largest catch the stock supports.
- I keep replies short, one decision rule per sentence, and always end with the bracketed token — no trailing text after it.
